system_prompt:
You are distilling one chapter of a guitar method book into a short summary.

The user will give you a chapter file with topic-organized verbatim quotes
plus the human-rationale notes for each. Write a one-paragraph summary (4-7
sentences) that captures:

  - what this chapter teaches (the techniques, concepts, rules, examples)
  - the master's characteristic moves visible in this chapter (if any)
  - the load-bearing terminology this chapter introduces

Reference the topic labels from the chapter file when useful. Do not invent
information not present in the chapter. If the chapter is biographical or
introductory rather than instructional, say so explicitly.

Output just the paragraph — no preamble, no JSON, no markdown formatting.

<<<CHAPTER FILE
# Chapter 9 — APPENDIX 2 - FINGERSTYLE TRAINING

_Pages 295-318._

> **Verbatim-quote constraint.** The quotes below are exact substrings of the raw transcript produced by `pdftotext`. The transcript may contain extraction artifacts where the book's typeface confuses the tool — e.g. `7irst` or `<irst` for `first`, `speci7ic` for `specific`. **Do NOT manually fix these in this file**: the quote-fidelity validator compares against the raw transcript, so a 'fixed' quote will fail verification and break Stage 2 idempotency. If a future pipeline iteration adds artifact-normalization, it must normalize the transcript and these files together.

## Preferred finger pairs for adjacent strings

> The main ways to pluck adjacent strings is with the p and i fingers, or i and m fingers.

**Significance (p. 298).** Defines the canonical two-finger combinations for multi-string plucking.

## Simultaneous note onset

> Regardless of which fingers you use, ensure that both fingers sound the notes simultaneously.

**Significance (p. 298).** Core synchronization rule separating clean ensemble fingerstyle from ragged arpeggiation.

## String-skip fingering for 6ths

> Now you need to negotiate a string skip in the plucking hand, hence the use of pm and ia as marked.

**Significance (p. 300).** Introduces the string-skip fingering rule specific to 6th intervals.

## Wrist position for multi-string plucking

> Ensure that your wrist is rolled slightly more towards the headstock to allow more space between the
> index finger and thumb.

**Significance (p. 298).** Foundational hand-position rule preventing mechanical failure when plucking adjacent strings.

## Three-note chord fingering preference

> 3 notes at once, it’s preferable to use pi m, or i ma, so it’s worth practicing both these
> combinations.

**Significance (p. 298).** Specifies preferred finger groupings for three-voice chords.

## Little finger usage and four-finger maximum

> I rarely use the little finger (c) on the right hand with fingerstyle technique — I tend to stick to 4-note
> voicings as a maximum

**Significance (p. 298).** Establishes a practical voicing ceiling and justifies omitting the weak little finger.

## Mirror use for technique development

> Using a mirror to see what your hand is doing when you’re developing techniques like these is very
> useful to check you're doing things correctly.

**Significance (p. 299).** Gives a concrete self-monitoring tool for catching hand-position errors.

## Thumb double-pluck technique

> Notice that the thumb plays a note twice in a row. It’s quite natural for the thumb to do a double
> pluck in these situations as it simplifies the picking fingering greatly.

**Significance (p. 301).** Legitimizes and explains the thumb double-pluck as a deliberate simplifying strategy.

## Relaxed hand for three-string exercises

> If you find these exercises a challenge, it would be worth revising the general tips on hand position
> and finger motion covered in the first lesson of this module.

**Significance (p. 303).** Reinforces relaxation as the corrective principle when coordination breaks down.

## Thumb independence in picking patterns

> thumb independence in a picking pattern context —- the thumb moves
> between the 5th and 4th strings as you play the exercise.

**Significance (p. 306).** Identifies thumb string-switching as a distinct skill targeted by the exercise.

## Bossa Nova etude practice sequence

> I would suggest practicing the picking pattern over a single chord for a while until you get it under
> your fingers first. After that, start to build the pattern over the full chord progression.

**Significance (p. 315).** Prescribes an isolation-then-integration practice sequence.

## Varying finger combinations on repeats

> For most of these exercises, I suggest you try another plucking finger combination on the repeats to
> help work out more picking combinations.

**Significance (p. 298).** Mandates alternate fingerings on repeats to expand picking vocabulary.
